pairs.a: atomic (merge_histograms, thread t of block B)

thread_relation: cross-block (the retiring block's late threads vs the last block)
thread_pair_example: block 3 thread 200 does its atomicAdd of its bins after thread 0 of block 3 has already executed atomicInc(finished_block_cnt) (finalize_pass L652-L660: __threadfence per thread, then thread 0's atomicInc with no __syncthreads); the last block then reads the same bin (volatile load) and zeroes it (plain store).
class_reason: atomic vs volatile load: both strong, unordered -> strong conflict (SC, D20); atomic vs plain store: not both strong -> data race (DR).
buggy_expected: SC for {merge_histograms atomicAdd, compute_bin_offsets volatile load} plus DR for {merge_histograms atomicAdd, init_histograms plain store}, in cross-block form on the global histogram.

fixed.reason: uncertain (verify.expected_report_fixed): the fix puts __syncthreads() after the per-thread __threadfence and before thread 0's atomicInc (finalize_pass, +2 lines); thread 0 therefore has fence -> atomicInc (a release pattern) but the last block has no acquire fence after its atomicInc (SASS: ATOMG.E.INC.STRONG.GPU then BAR.RED.OR then the volatile loads, no MEMBAR in between), so a strict PTX reading may keep the SC report; a detector that treats fence+atomic as release/acquire hand-off reports nothing. T21b triages a fixed-build report here against this note, it is not a false positive by default.
